related_questions.question: What are the requirements to enter Canada from the United States?

text_blocks.snippet: To travel to Canada from the US, you'll generally need a valid U.S. passport or passport card. However, depending on your mode of transportation and citizenship, other documents like a birth certificate, Enhanced Driver's License, or Nexus card may also be acceptable. You might also need an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) if flying, according to Canada.ca.
snippet_highlighted_words: a valid U.S. passport or passport card

list.title: Passport or Passport Card:
list.snippet: A valid U.S. passport or passport card is the most common and recommended document.

list.title: Enhanced Driver's License:
list.snippet: In some cases, an Enhanced Driver's License (issued by certain states like New York, Michigan, Minnesota, Vermont, and Washington) can be used at land border crossings.

list.title: Nexus Card:
list.snippet: A NEXUS card, which is a trusted traveler program card, can also be used for entry into Canada, including at airports.

list.title: Birth Certificate and Photo ID:
list.snippet: In some cases, a birth certificate and a government-issued photo ID (like a driver's license) may be accepted at land border crossings.

list.title: eTA (if flying):
list.snippet: If you're flying to Canada, you'll likely need an eTA in addition to your passport.
Valid Passport: A valid passport from your country of citizenship is required.
Visa or eTA: Depending on your citizenship, you may also need a Canadian visitor visa or an eTA.
Other Documents: You may also need to provide other documents, such as proof of financial means, and proof of ties to your home country.

list.title: Return to the U.S.:
list.snippet: When returning to the U.S. from Canada, you may need more specific documentation than when entering Canada.

list.title: Entry Requirements:
list.snippet: It's always a good idea to check the specific entry requirements for Canada before your trip, as they can vary based on your citizenship and other factors.

text_blocks.snippet: For the most up-to-date information, always check the official websites of the Canadian government (like Canada Border Services Agency or Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada) and the U.S. Department of State.
